```{r}
#| label: packages
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)

life <- readr::read_csv("../data/lifeexpectancy_infant.csv")
regmapping <- readr::read_csv("../data/loc.csv")

lifespan <- life %>%
  left_join(regmapping, by = "location")

lifeexpwide <- lifespan %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = lifeexp
  )

lifeexpwide2023 <- lifespan %>%
  filter(year == 2023) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = lifeexp
  )
```

## ggplot2 $\in$ tidyverse

:::: {.columns .v-center}

::: {.column width="40%"}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: 80%

knitr::include_graphics("../img/ggplot2-part-of-tidyverse.png")
```

:::

::: {.column width="60%"}

- **ggplot2** is the tidyverse's data visualization package.
- The structure of ggplot code can be summarized as:

```{r}
#| eval: false

ggplot(
  data = my_data,
  mapping = aes(
    x = x_var,
    y = y_var
  )
) +
  geom_xxx() +
  other_options
```

:::

## Data: Life expectancy from infancy

IHME data on location (mostly countries), World Bank region, binary sex, and estimated life expectancy and population in 2023 will be used to explore the men's health gap (later we will add more years).

:::: {.columns .v-center}

::: {.column width="30%"}

```{r}

#| out-width: 50%

```


## Life expectancy

:::: columns

::: {.column width="70%"}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-align: center

ggplot(
  data = lifeexpwide2023,
  mapping = aes(
    x = Female,
    y = Male,
    color = worldbankregion
  )
) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Life expectancy",
    subtitle = "2023",
    x = "Female life expectancy",
    y = "Male life expectancy",
    color = "World Bank Region"
  )
```

:::

# Aesthetics

---

## Aesthetics options

Commonly used characteristics of plotting characters that can be **mapped to a specific variable** in the data are:

::: {.incremental}

- `color`
- `shape`
- `size`
- `alpha` (transparency)

:::

---

## Color

:::: columns

::: {.column width="40%"}

```{r}
#| eval: false

  )
) +
  geom_point()
```

## Shape, take 2

:::: columns

```{r}
#| eval: false

ggplot(
  lifeexpwide2023,
  aes(

    shape = worldbankregion
  )
) +
  geom_point() +  
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16,17,15,18,3,4,8,0,1,2))
```

## Shape

Can also map to the same variable as `color` (helps for color vision deficiency)

## Mapping vs. setting aesthetics

:::: columns

::: {.column width="50%"}

**Mapping**

<div style="font-size:0.80em;">


```{r}
#| warning: false
#| out-width: 100%

ggplot(
  lifeexpwide2023,
  aes(
    x = Female,
    y = Male,
    size = pop
  )
) +
  geom_point()
```

</div>

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

**Setting**

<div style="font-size:0.80em;">


```{r}
#| warning: false
#| out-width: 100%

ggplot(
  lifeexpwide2023,
  aes(
    x = Female,
    y = Male
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 2)
```

</div>

:::

::::

---

## Mapping vs. setting

- **Mapping:** Determine the size, alpha, etc. of points based on the values of a variable in the data.
  - Goes into `aes()`.

- **Setting:** Determine the size, alpha, etc. of points **not** based on the values of a variable in the data.
  - Goes into `geom_*()` (this was `geom_point()` in the previous example, but we'll learn about other geoms soon!).
  
---

# Faceting

---

## Faceting

- Smaller plots that display different subsets of the data
- Useful for exploring conditional relationships and large data

---

## Faceting

:::: columns

::: {.column width="50%"}

```{r}
#| eval: false

lifeexpwide %>%
  filter(
    year %in% c(1999, 2009, 2023),
    worldbankregion %in% c(
      "North America",
      "South Asia",
      "Sub-Saharan Africa"
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = Female,
      y = Male
    )
  ) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(year ~ worldbankregion)
```

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| out-width: 100%

lifeexpwide %>%
  filter(
    year %in% c(1999, 2010, 2023),
    worldbankregion %in% c(
      "North America",
      "South Asia",
      "Sub-Saharan Africa"
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = Female,
      y = Male
    )
  ) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(year ~ worldbankregion)
```

:::

::::

---

## Various ways to facet

---

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| fig-asp: 0.5

lifeexpwide %>%
  filter(
    year %in% c(1999, 2010, 2023),
    worldbankregion %in% c("North America","South Asia","Sub-Saharan Africa"
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(x = Female, y = Male)
  ) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~worldbankregion)
```

---

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| fig-asp: 0.5

lifeexpwide %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1999, 2010, 2023),worldbankregion %in% c("North America","South Asia","Sub-Saharan Africa")) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = Female,
               y = Male)) + 
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(.~worldbankregion)
```

---

## Faceting summary

- `facet_grid()`
  - 2D grid
  - `rows ~ cols`
  - Use `.` for no split.

- `facet_wrap()`
  - 1D ribbon wrapped according to the number of rows and columns specified or the available plotting area.
  
---

```{r}
  geom_point() +
```
```{r}
  facet_wrap(~worldbankregion) +
  guides(color = "none")
```
